The accidental release prevention and emergency response policies at the stationary source [40 CFR 68.155(a)]:

The Scout storage tank facility, under Scout Energy Partners (Scout EP), is strongly committed to the safety of the employees, the public and the environment. This commitment is demonstrated through our comprehensive accidental release prevention program, which covers design, installation, operating procedures, maintenance, and employee training. Robust engineering controls are in place to prevent potential releases of regulated substances. As a non-responding facility for releases of RMP-listed chemicals, the site utilizes an Emergency Action Plan.

The stationary source and regulated substances handled [40 CFR 68.155(b)]:

The storage tank facility located in Masterson, Texas consists of a tank (TK-1007) that stores a flammable mixture (stabilized condensate), a combustor, and a truck loading manifold for loading condensate into tanker trucks for distribution, along with ancillary piping. The stabilized condensate is a byproduct of natural gas processing at the Fain gas plant and is transported to the storage tank via an underground pipeline.

The general accidental release prevention program and chemical-specific prevention steps [40 CFR 68.155(c)]:

The storage tank facility is not required to implement the Program Level 3 prevention program requirements under the RMP regulations because they are eligible for RMP Program Level 1. However, the facility will still ensure compliance with the necessary safety requirements to prevent or minimize the consequences of catastrophic releases of flammable or explosive chemicals. This includes proper hazard identification, facility design and maintenance, and consequence minimization through an effective Emergency Action Plan. Scout EP has a program in place to ensure their condensate storage facility complies with these requirements and specific regulations.

The five-year accident history [40 CFR 68.155(d)]:

Th

ere have been no RMP-reportable accidents within the last five (5) years at the condensate storage tank facility.

The emergency response program [40 CFR 68.155(e)]:

The emergency response program for this facility is contained in the Masterson Facility Emergency Action Plan (EAP) document. A copy of the EAP has been provided to the Local Emergency Planning Committee of Potter/Randal County. The EAP includes steps to take in case of an uncontrolled release of hazardous substance. The initial step would be to contact the Potter/Randall County Emergency Response system which in turn will contact other emergency response agencies to aid in controlling access to the facility by the public. 

Planned changes to improve safety [40 CFR 68.155(f)]:

Scout EP is continually working with their team to improve safety at their facility. They will work with their management team to ensure concerns or changes are addressed appropriately for the safety of their workers and community. 

The condensate storage tank facility has completed this report to provide the public with information about our activities at this facility. We believe that the numerous controls in place to maintain a safe operation, combined with our commitment to continuous improvement, make it unlikely that an incident affecting our employees or the surrounding area will occur.
